scope: Manual care reference for the seven requested leaf names and two issues only. Not an expansion of the image classifier.

tomato_early_blight.summary: Manage confirmed Early Blight and protect healthy growth; dead or spotted tissue will not turn healthy again.
tomato_early_blight.evidence_note: General tomato guidance. These sources do not establish different treatment rates or resistance for the six named tomato varieties.
start_steps: Confirm the diagnosis: Early Blight commonly starts on older lower leaves with brown spots and concentric rings. Similar-looking problems require local agricultural advice.
When foliage is dry, remove badly affected lower leaves without stripping the plant. Bag diseased debris and clean cutting tools before moving to another plant.
Mulch bare soil, support the plant, improve spacing and water at the soil surface to reduce splash onto leaves.
organic_steps: Choose a copper fungicide labelled for tomato Early Blight and approved for your organic production standard. Organic approval is product-specific; copper is still a pesticide.
Use it early to protect healthy foliage. Follow the preparation and spraying method below and the exact product label; it does not repair established lesions.
chemical_steps: As an alternative, use a locally registered tomato Early Blight fungicide, such as chlorothalonil only where the current label permits this crop and disease.
Apply at the label rate, coverage and repeat interval. Observe its maximum applications, re-entry interval and pre-harvest interval; do not automatically combine it with the organic option.
follow_up_steps: Record the product, dose and application date. Inspect new growth between treatments; follow the label for repeat spraying rather than increasing the concentration.
If disease continues to spread rapidly, ask a local agricultural extension service to verify the diagnosis and management plan.

tomato_powdery_mildew.summary: Suppress confirmed Powdery Mildew and protect new foliage; this is management guidance, not a guaranteed cure.
tomato_powdery_mildew.evidence_note: General tomato/vegetable guidance; no variety-specific efficacy or dose is established here.
start_steps: Confirm Powdery Mildew: white powdery patches can develop on leaves, but some tomato infections mainly cause yellow patches. Seek advice if the symptoms do not match.
Remove a few heavily affected leaves, give plants suitable sunlight and improve airflow without over-pruning. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer.
organic_steps: For a mild confirmed infection, choose an organically approved neem-oil fungicide explicitly labelled for tomato Powdery Mildew. Follow its instructions and test a small area if the label directs.

Cover the affected and susceptible leaf surfaces as directed, during cool suitable conditions. Avoid oils on heat- or water-stressed plants and when temperatures exceed about 32°C (90°F), or any stricter label limit.
chemical_steps: As an alternative, use tomato-labelled wettable sulfur primarily to prevent new infections or protect new foliage; it should not be described as repairing an established infection.
Do not mix sulfur with oil sprays. Separate them by at least two weeks, or longer if either label requires; avoid sulfur near or above 32°C (90°F) and on stressed plants.
follow_up_steps: Recheck new growth and powdery patches between applications. Repeat only at the product label interval and respect the harvest/re-entry restrictions.
Persistent or severe infection needs local crop-specific advice; do not add stronger doses or homemade detergents.

tulsi_early_blight.summary: Diagnosis requires confirmation: do not automatically transfer tomato Early Blight to Holy Basil (Tulsi).
tulsi_early_blight.evidence_note: Available basil references discuss several leaf-spot diseases and primarily concern sweet basil (Ocimum basilicum), not confirmed tomato-type Early Blight on Tulsi (Ocimum tenuiflorum). This entry is not a validated Tulsi disease-treatment pairing.
start_steps: Take clear photos of both leaf surfaces and the whole plant; ask a local agricultural extension service to identify the cause before using a fungicide.
Remove a few affected leaves with clean tools, avoid handling wet foliage, improve airflow and water at the base.
organic_steps: Use sanitation and growing-condition changes first. A biological/organic pesticide is an option only if its current local label explicitly covers Tulsi and the identified disease.
A product labelled for tomatoes, ornamental plants or sweet basil is not automatically authorised for Tulsi; obtain crop-specific advice before applying it.
chemical_steps: There is no verified exact chemical cure provided for this Tulsi/Early Blight combination. Do not apply the tomato treatment schedule to Tulsi.
After diagnosis, use a chemical fungicide only when locally registered for Tulsi and that disease, following its application, re-entry and edible-leaf harvest restrictions.
follow_up_steps: Keep a record of symptoms and any treatment. Monitor new growth and avoid harvesting treated leaves until the relevant label permits it.

tulsi_powdery_mildew.summary: Confirm Powdery Mildew on Tulsi before selecting a product; general basil information is not a Tulsi pesticide approval.
tulsi_powdery_mildew.evidence_note: Crop-specific product registration and efficacy for Holy Basil are not established by this lookup. Sweet-basil advice must not be assumed to apply to Tulsi.
start_steps: Have white growth or yellowing checked if the diagnosis is uncertain; appearance alone does not establish the organism.
Remove heavily affected leaves sparingly, improve light and airflow, and avoid excessive nitrogen or prolonged leaf wetness.
organic_steps: Use cultural measures first. An organically approved biological fungicide is an option only when its label specifically permits Tulsi and Powdery Mildew.
Do not substitute homemade soap, baking-soda or neem mixtures for a registered product; edible herb leaves can be injured or left with unsuitable residues.
chemical_steps: A formulated fungicide such as potassium bicarbonate may be considered only if the current local label explicitly lists Tulsi and Powdery Mildew; this lookup does not establish that such a product is registered locally.
If no suitable Tulsi-labelled product is available, continue nonchemical management and obtain local extension advice rather than borrowing tomato or ornamental-plant instructions.
follow_up_steps: Recheck new leaves after management changes. For any labelled treatment, follow the repeat interval and edible-leaf harvest restrictions; washing does not replace the pre-harvest interval.

application_steps: Read the complete current label before buying or opening the product: crop, disease, dilution, mixing order, coverage, maximum applications, harvest waiting period and re-entry requirements must all match.
Wear the label-required protective equipment and keep children and animals away. Use dedicated measuring equipment and a clean sprayer; do not use kitchen utensils.

For a concentrate requiring dilution, measure the label dose for the chosen water volume and follow the stated mixing order. If the label gives a per-litre rate, required product = label rate × litres of water; do not dilute a ready-to-use product unless directed.
Spray only the plant parts and surfaces specified by the label, evenly and without drift. Choose suitable calm conditions and respect heat/rain restrictions, especially for oil and sulfur products.
Choose one suitable treatment route rather than mixing organic and chemical products. Tank-mix only when both labels explicitly allow the combination and crop.
Clean the equipment and dispose of leftovers as the label instructs, away from drains or water sources. Record the treatment and follow its re-entry and pre-harvest intervals.
